new_entities.name: Topical rosemary oil
new_entities.description: Topical rosemary oil used as a non-prescription hair-growth intervention.

new_entities.name: Androgenetic alopecia
new_entities.description: Pattern hair loss in men or women.

edges.effect_quant: The only well-known randomized comparative trial found rosemary oil and minoxidil 2% both improved hair count by 6 months without a significant between-group difference. That keeps the signal interesting but too thin to present as an established, prescription-grade hair-loss therapy.
edges.population: adults with androgenetic alopecia using topical rosemary oil preparations for several months
edges.mechanism: Rosemary oil has been proposed to influence microcirculation and local inflammatory tone, but the human hair-regrowth mechanism remains more speculative than proven.
edges.summary: Topical rosemary oil is better described as a plausible low-confidence alternative than a validated mainstay. One trial suggests it may help, but the literature is sparse and far behind the evidence base for minoxidil or finasteride.
edges.caveats: This is exactly the kind of consumer hair-loss edge that should be labeled cautiously. A single positive comparative study and a few broad reviews are not enough to treat rosemary oil as equivalent to standard therapy.

evidence.notes: Rosemary oil vs minoxidil 2% for the treatment of androgenetic alopecia: a randomized comparative trial.
